holidays.name: National Onion Ring Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the crispy, golden, battered hoop of joy. Order a basket at your favorite diner, dunk the rings in a sauce, and see how many you can wear on your fingers before you eat them.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. Its creator is unclear, and it has spread through food-holiday calendars over the years.
holidays.funFact: Onion rings are often served in a stack, and the tallest ones are called 'onion towers'. Many restaurants now serve them that way.

holidays.name: National Kissing Day
holidays.description: A day for smooching. It covers a peck on the cheek, a big romantic kiss, and a smooch on a pet's head. Pucker up and spread some affection.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is listed among the lighthearted days of late June.
holidays.funFact: The scientific study of kissing is called philematology. Researchers in the field look at the biology and psychology behind a kiss.

holidays.name: World Rainforest Day
holidays.description: A global day to celebrate the planet's rainforests and the many species that live in them. People mark it by learning about rainforest conservation, supporting protection efforts, and sharing the cause online.
holidays.origin: The day was launched in 2017 by the Rainforest Partnership, an environmental nonprofit. It aims to build awareness and encourage action to protect rainforests.
holidays.funFact: Rainforests cover only about 6% of Earth's land surface. Scientists estimate they are home to more than half of the world's plant and animal species.
